_README: TRANSLITERATION ALTERNATIONS FOR WEST AFRICAN NAMES.
OWNER: this file is seeded with a best-effort starting set and is meant to
be expanded by you. It is plain data — no code changes are needed to add a
rule, and every rule you add is picked up by the next `npm run
ingest:variants`.
Each rule rewrites a substring of a normalised (uppercased, de-accented)
name. `bidirectional: true` means the substitution is also applied in
reverse, which is usually what you want: if CHUKWU can be spelled CHUKU,
then a customer who writes CHUKU should match a list entry spelled CHUKWU.
`position` constrains where the rule may fire:
'any'    - anywhere in a name token (default)
'start'  - only at the beginning of a token
'end'    - only at the end of a token
Keep rules narrow. A rule like E->I applied anywhere generates enormous
numbers of useless variants and inflates the candidate set, which is the
exact problem this product exists to reduce. Prefer a longer, more
specific pattern over a single-letter one.
Sources to draw on when expanding: Onwu orthography for Igbo, the Yoruba
alphabet's underdotted characters (s-dot -> S or SH, e-dot, o-dot), and
Hausa Boko spellings of Arabic-derived names.

rules.note: CHUKWUEMEKA / CHUKUEMEKA, NWACHUKWU / NWACHUKU. The single most common Igbo alternation. Note the pattern is KWU->KU, not KW->KU: the W is dropped and the U retained, so a KW->KU rule would produce the nonsense CHUKUUEMEKA.
CHINEDU / CINEDU. Restricted to token start to avoid mangling -CH- medially.
Yoruba s-dot is romanised as either S or SH. SHOLA / SOLA, ADESHINA / ADESINA.
The highest-frequency name on earth and the most variably spelled. Whole-token rule rather than letter-level, deliberately.
IFY / IFI, CHY / CHI. Token-final only.
OLUWASEUN / OLUSEUN. The theophoric prefix contracts.
